 This petition coming on for admission this day, the cou  the following:
 ORDER Heard finally, with the consent of the parties. 2] This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Article 226 seeking the following reliefs:-
"(i) Issue a writ, direction or order in the nature of CERTIORARI or other appropriate writ, calling for the records of the petitioner's case.

(ii) Issue a writ, direction or order in the nature of CERTIORARI /MANDAMUS or other appropriate writ, directing the respondent to decide the complaint of the petitioner and cancel the certificate of the respondent no. 6.
(iii) Award the costs of the petition and (iv) Grant such other relief or reliefs as this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the facts and circumstances of the case."

3] The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.6 Sawera Jaiswal has forged her Caste Certificate, on the basis of which, she has also contested the election of Nagar Panchayat, Rajgarh,
District Dhar, and to find out the veracity of the aforesaid Caste Certificate, the petitioner has already made a complaint to the S.P., Dhar with a copy to the Collector.
Thus, it is submitted that the respondent No.3 be directed to decided the petitioner's application at the earliest.

4] Counsel appearing for the respondent No.6 has vehemently opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the petitioner had earlier approached this Court in W.P. 9875/2023, whereby, the petitioner was directed to take recourse of the appropriate legal remedy available to her, and thus,
the election petition was filed in the Court of Additional District Judge, Sardarpur, which has Anjali Jaiswal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76813243/
2 already been dismissed on 23.07.2023, and that order has not been challenged by the petitioner,
and has attained the finality.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the petitioner has also resorted to file a private complaint under Section 200 of the Cr.P.C., under Section 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the IPC, in which, even the complainant's evidence has not yet been recorded, despite the fact that the complaint was filed on 23.06.2023.
Thus, it is submitted that since the private complaint has already been filed, no further order is required to be passed in this case.
5] Counsel for the respondent/State has submitted that they have already forwarded the petitioner's complaint to the Collector, who is the competent to pass the order and the petition is premature.

6]
Heard.

Having considered the rival submissions, on perusal of the documents filed on record and taking note of the fact that the petitioner has also filed a private complaint in the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Sardarpur, District Dhar, this Court is inclined to dispose of this writ petition with a direction to the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Sardarpur, District Dhar to decide the complaint filed by the petitioner expeditiously, preferably, within a period of six months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
7] It is made clear that this Court has not reflected upon the merits of the case.
